title: Enterprise proxy onboarding prioritization matrix and safe-fastpath
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise customers frequently submit model requests that span new model additions, urgent version pinning, and deprecation exceptions. Current intake is ad-hoc: high-visibility customers get manual fast-tracks, while smaller-but-regulated customers wait longer than SLA. Goal: design and operationalize a lightweight prioritization matrix (the 'proxy') that converts customer signals + product constraints into a deterministic lane assignment and safe-fastpath rules for expedited onboarding or pinning. Scope: matrix covers new model adds, variant pin requests, temporary pin extensions, and scheduled deprecations. It must include explicit eval-gate mapping, minimum telemetry required for canary, and rollback/fallback prescriptions. Out of scope: full automation of model quality scoring (research will continue independently), and on-prem installation steps (handled by Private team).
acceptance_criteria: A1: A prioritization matrix doc that maps request vectors (customer tier, compliance needs, latency/cost sensitivity, model novelty, security flags) to lanes (Standard, Enterprise Fastpath, Compliance Review, Blocked).
A2: Clear safe-fastpath checklist for Enterprise Fastpath that includes mandatory smoke evals, minimum prompt set, SLA for rollback, and required sign-offs (PM + Runtime + Security).
A3: Triage playbook for pinning requests describing conditions for temporary pin vs permanent pin, expiration policy, and auto-notification cadence to customers.
A4: Example routing rules expressible as configuration snippets for the Catalog router (3 prioritized rules).
A5: Stakeholder sign-off from Runtime, Security, and Solutions within the cycle and a staging pilot with two active customer requests executed end-to-end.

risks: R1: Fastpath without strict canary/eval gates could cause unnoticed quality regressions for customers with high SLAs.
R2: Overly permissive pinning policies increase catalog maintenance cost and technical debt during deprecations.
R3: Security/KMS requirements for private variants could delay fastpath by multiple weeks if not triaged early.
tradeoffs: T1: Tighter eval gates increase time-to-onboard but reduce customer-facing regressions; recommended default: short focused eval set for fastpath (15 prompts) and extended eval for Standard lane.
T2: Automating routing vs manual adjudication: automation scales but requires upfront signals instrumentation; initial roll will be semi-automated with human-in-loop for edge cases.
T3: Support burden vs acquisition: enabling a fast Enterprise lane increases sales velocity but requires a staffed on-call rotation for rollback and post-mortems.
implementation_notes: Step 1: Finalize v0 matrix doc and three routing rule examples (PM/Runtime/Security).
Step 2: Add 'fastpath' flag to catalog intake form and Console UI prototype (Design).
Step 3: Implement pilot routing rules in staging and run end-to-end with two customers for 14 days.
Step 4: Measure pilot metrics (time-to-approve, incidents, regression rate) and iterate; hand over to Operations for runbook creation.
notes: Unique to this ticket: framing the prioritization as a 'proxy' that outputs lane + safe-fastpath checklist, rather than attempting to score requests numerically. This reduces churn on intake form fields and focuses engineering effort on deterministic routing rules and a short, auditable fastpath checklist.
